title: Smart Sleeve for Psychiatric Conditions (OCD, and Others)
summary: The goal of this study is to test the feasibility of a wearable sleeve device. For patients with OCD who enroll in this study, ERP (exposure and response prevention) therapy will be provided through the study, free of charge. The sleeve is a MXene and silicone device worn on the forearm which measures muscle activity, heart rate, arm position, and other physiological markers. Our hope is that the data collected by the sleeve will correlate with psychiatric scales collected by our clinical psychology team, which will enable us to measure these conditions using the sleeve alone.
criteria:
Subjects must meet all of the following criteria to be eligible for the study:

1. 18-60 years old.
2. Presence of a clinically diagnosed psychiatric disorder with maladaptive behavior according to the DSM-5.
3. Presence of clinically significant symptoms relevant to the participant's diagnosis.
4. Ability to understand procedure-related instructions and complete study assessments in English, in the opinion of the Principal Investigator.
5. Willingness and ability to comply with protocol requirements (e.g., visits, evaluations), in the opinion of the Principal Investigator.
6. Willingness and ability to provide written agreement to allow communication between the research team and the participant's treating clinician(s).
7. Willingness and ability to provide informed consent, in the opinion of the Principal Investigator.

Age is restricted to 18-60 to focus the pilot on an adult population with sufficient physical mobility for sleeve wear; no exclusions are made on the basis of gender, race, or ethnicity, and the distribution of participants is expected to be equitable across these categories.

Individuals meeting any of the following criteria will be excluded from the study:

1. Hearing loss that, in the opinion of the PI, an audiologist, or a treating physician, is likely to affect the subject's ability to comply with study requirements or may affect data integrity.
2. Pregnancy (by self-report). This criterion is conservative rather than based on a known contraindication: study procedures may intentionally increase anxiety to evaluate strategies for provoking and then reducing distress, and the team has elected to exclude pregnant individuals from this pilot out of caution.
3. Any past or present medical condition, disease, disorder, or injury that, in the opinion of the PI, may reduce or hinder the subject's ability to comply with study requirements or may affect the integrity of the data or results.
4. Previous injury or surgery affecting nerve distribution in the sleeve-wearing limb.
5. Nerve damage (neuropathy).
6. A diagnosed neuromuscular disorder.
7. A pacemaker.
8. A history of skin allergies, psoriasis, eczema, dermatitis, or other skin-inflammation conditions.

Participation in ongoing therapy or use of psychiatric medication is not an exclusion criterion.
